findings.evidence: Lines 184-188 define `mapWalk := (f.mapPath (p.toBidirected x.2)).toGraphWalk`. Every lemma about it after line 190 is proved by unfolding `mapWalk`; there is no stated bridge to `mapPath`.
findings.fix: Add `theorem toBidirected_mapWalk (f) (p : G.Walk x y) : (f.mapWalk p).toBidirected (f.vertexEquiv x).2 = f.mapPath (p.toBidirected x.2)`, possibly with a `mapWalk_def`/`toGraphWalk_mapPath` restatement, and drop `@[expose]` from `mapWalk`.
findings.issue: `mapWalk` is `@[expose]` and is defined via `mapPath ∘ toBidirected`, but nothing states that link as a lemma. Downstream flow reductions, which the PR says will reuse this transport, would have to unfold `mapWalk`. `isCycle_mapWalk` unfolds it with `simp only [mapWalk, Walk.toBidirected_toGraphWalk, ...]` for exactly this reason.

findings.evidence: The diff contains no out-of-module use of these definitions; `grep` finds `mapWalk`/`mapPath` only in the new file.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from `mapHom`, `toPrefunctor` and `mapPath`. If a definitional fact is needed downstream, state it as a `(rfl)` lemma instead.
findings.issue: The same over-exposure occurs on `mapHom` (l.41), `toPrefunctor` (l.54) and `mapPath` (l.90). Their only unfoldings (`simp [toPrefunctor, mapHom]` and the `(rfl)` proofs) are in this same module, and `mapHom_fst`, `toPrefunctor_obj/map` and `mapPath_nil/cons/comp` already characterize them.

findings.evidence: `grep 'copy_copy|length_copy|support_copy'` under `TauCeti/Combinatorics/Graph` returns no hits; only `copy_rfl_rfl`, `copy_nil` and `copy_cons` exist (Basic.lean l.63-79).
findings.fix: Add the standard copy API: `copy_copy`, `length_copy`, `support_copy`, `edges_copy`, `isTrail_copy`, `isPath_copy`, `isCycle_copy` (or a `copy` reachability form), and `append_copy_copy`/`reverse_copy`, all `@[simp]`.
findings.issue: `Walk.copy` is new public API, and `mapWalk_refl`, `mapWalk_trans`, `mapWalk_symm_mapWalk` and `mapWalk_mapWalk_symm` are all stated through it. It ships only `copy_rfl_rfl`, `copy_nil` and `copy_cons`, so consumers cannot move length, support, edges, trail/path/cycle predicates or append across a `copy` without unfolding it.

summary: Walk transport bodies (`mapHom`, `toPrefunctor`, `mapPath`, `mapWalk`) are `@[expose]`d although every consumer use is covered by lemmas, except a missing `mapWalk`/`toBidirected` bridge lemma. The new `Walk.copy`, in which the identity, composition and inverse laws are stated, lacks its characteristic API.
